content_md:
[Kris Abdelmessih](https://moontowermeta.com/)'s example inspired me to vibe code [useful little financial calculations](/crypto-fixed-income-modeling/) into open sourced [mini web apps](https://mstr.artlu.xyz/). They would have otherwise lived in harder-to-share, harder-to-maintain Excel spreadsheets (VBA) or Jupyter notebooks (Python).

In a [solo episode of Manifold podcast](https://www.manifold1.com/episodes/theoretical-physics-with-generative-ai-101), Steve Hsu describes how he performs theoretical physics research using multiple AI models. Interesting to hear an avid LLM user's experience, with over 40 years as a professional scientist.

After listening to Professor Hsu's approach, as well as [Dialectic with Jackson Dahl's talk](https://jdahl.substack.com/p/cursors-ryo-lu-on-soulful-design) with Cursor's Head of Design Ryo Lu, I asked 6 AI models to verify my vibe coded Black-Scholes implementation. Cursor provides a nice harness to manage parallel reviews. I can verify that different models take entirely different approaches, and inspect their conclusions.

This is a textbook ask, far from asking an LLM to perform theoretical physics. I had already visually inspected the code, and would expect any first-year quant on
